title: Monoidal comparison for the specified finite-coefficient hearts
statement:
For a scheme X and a finite discrete commutative topological ring A, the specified integralModelIntrinsicRealization is an equivalence. There is an additive equivalence H from intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves to modules over the constant lifted A-ring on the coefficient-sized site, such that finiteHeartRealization of [lem-sfb-embedded-finite-heart-realization] followed by H is strong monoidal for the existing tensors. There is no derived or constructibility assertion.

Exact Lean assertion:
theorem finiteHeartMonoidalPresentation
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type) [CommRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A] :
    letI : HasSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} :=
      CategoryTheory.siteAbelianHasSheafify.{u + 1, u, u + 1} _
    letI : (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} :=
      CategoryTheory.siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective.{u + 1, u, u + 1} _
    let R := ConstantCompletion.constant
      (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} X) (ULift.{u + 1, 0} A)
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    (integralModelIntrinsicRealization X A).IsEquivalence ∧
      ∃ H : Scheme.proEtaleRingModules X
          (Scheme.proEtaleConstantRing X (ULift.{u, 0} A)) ≌ ConstantCompletion.Mod R,
        ∃ (_ : H.functor.Additive),
          Nonempty (finiteHeartRealization X A ⋙ H.functor).Monoidal

proof.text: Define the constant-function ring presheaf map from the double lift of A to U ↦ C(U,A). It is locally surjective on the open fibres of each continuous discrete-valued function. Two distinct constants agree only on the empty scheme, covered by the empty family. Apply the existing associated-module-sheaf equivalence argument to this locally bijective map. Its unit, on the original sheaf of fixed-scalar modules, is an invertible natural transformation into the composite with integralModelFixedScalars: the scalar maps agree sectionwise. Cancel the associated-module-sheaf equivalence to prove that this specified fixed-scalar functor is an equivalence. Compose with continuousRingModuleEquivalence and finiteCoefficientIntrinsicRealization to prove the first conjunct.

Use the existing finiteComparisonRealization P and coefficient model realization Q. The private finiteRealizationMonoidal_exists and proRealization_monoidal proofs in finiteComparisonPresentation supply their strong monoidal structures from section tensor comparison, scalar-isomorphism transport, constant scalar restriction and site transport. Set K = P inverse followed by Q inverse; K is an additive strong monoidal equivalence from continuous internal modules to the coefficient model. No new tensor comparison or local scalar identification is asserted.

Write I for the specified intrinsic realization, now proved an equivalence, and S for extension along finiteScalarMap. Set H = I inverse followed by K. The inverse of the unit of I identifies (S followed by I) followed by H with S followed by K. Extension S is strong monoidal since its scalar map is invertible, and K is strong monoidal by the preceding step. Transport this structure through the displayed natural isomorphism. Additivity of H follows from equivalence and binary products. This proves the exact unchanged existential conclusion.
